data.title: SpaceX Expands NASA Contract With Three More Crew Flights Through 2030
data.description: According to CNBC, SpaceX has expanded its contract with NASA and will carry out three additional crewed Dragon flights to the International Space Station through 2030, with the work worth up to $946 million if completed. The award lifts SpaceX's total missions under NASA's Commercial Crew Transportation Capability contract to 17 operational flights, and NASA said the deal helps it maintain access to the station with two commercial crew providers. SpaceX will handle ground, launch, in-orbit, cargo transport, and return and recovery operations, along with lifeboat capability while docked to the ISS. Under the contract, SpaceX will have earned $5.92 billion from NASA. NASA said Crew 13 is expected to launch in October and Crew 14 is slated for next spring.

data.description:

data.title: Pentagon Tells Congress U.S. Iran-Related Spending Has Reached $43.6 Billion
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, the Pentagon told Congress that U.S. spending on Iran-related operations has reached $43.6 billion so far, including about $11.2 billion for incremental operation costs, about $28.1 billion to replenish expended munitions, and about $4.3 billion to replace lost equipment.

data.title: STOCKS | AAII Sentiment Falls to 16-Month Low
data.description:
Investor sentiment dropped to its lowest level in 16 months, according to Bloomberg, as the American Association of Individual Investors' weekly survey showed.

Oil prices stayed elevated while the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since 2023.

data.title: STOCKS | UBS's Lovell Says Earnings, Not Fed, Are Driving Stocks
data.description:
Nadia Lovell, head of global equity strategy at UBS Global Wealth Management, said strong earnings and broadening profit growth should keep stocks moving higher even as rising rates create near-term volatility, according to Bloomberg.

Speaking on "Bloomberg Surveillance," Lovell said earnings, not valuation expansion, will drive the market.

data.title: STOCKS | General Motors Bets on Diesel Range for Redesigned Silverado and Sierra
data.description:
General Motors will launch redesigned 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 and GMC Sierra 1500 pickups in the fourth quarter. According to Sina Finance, the two models will continue to offer a 3.0-liter Duramax inline-six diesel engine and an optional 34-gallon fuel tank, giving them a highway range of more than 900 miles.

The new Duramax diesel still produces 305 horsepower and 495 pound-feet of torque. General Motors said it adjusted the pistons, turbo guide vanes, fuel injection system, and nitrogen oxide sensors, and increased the diesel exhaust fluid tank by about 2 gallons to extend the distance between refills.

Based on highway fuel economy of about 27 miles per gallon for the two-wheel-drive version, the 34-gallon tank implies a theoretical range of about 918 miles. General Motors said actual range will still depend on payload, towing weight, drivetrain, speed, and ambient temperature.

The diesel version is positioned for long-distance efficiency rather than maximum towing power. The Silverado diesel can tow up to 12,000 pounds, while the Sierra diesel can tow about 12,100 pounds. Both are below the peak figures for models equipped with the 5.7-liter V8 engine.

The new Silverado and Sierra will keep four engine options in total. The entry-level 2.7-liter TurboMax turbocharged four-cylinder rises to 350 horsepower and 455 pound-feet, the new 5.7-liter V8 delivers 402 horsepower and 428 pound-feet, and the 6.6-liter V8 reaches 481 horsepower and 501 pound-feet. All four engines are paired with a 10-speed automatic transmission.

data.title: Allen Media Group CEO Byron Allen Emphasizes Deleveraging as Loan Trades Near Lows
data.description:
Allen Media Group Chief Executive Officer Byron Allen said the company is focused on deleveraging in a recent call with investors, according to people familiar with the matter.

He did not address how the media firm plans to handle looming debt maturities, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: STOCKS | Fed overnight reverse repo usage rises to $576 million
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Federal Reserve overnight reverse repo facility usage was $576 million on Friday, with three counterparties, up from $276 million in the previous trading day.

data.title: STOCKS | European Shares Extend Losses as Volkswagen Cuts Outlook
data.description:
European shares extended their losses as auto stocks fell after Volkswagen cut its profit outlook, dragging the broader market lower. According to Sina Finance, the Stoxx Europe 600 closed down 1%, fell 0.6% for the week, and posted a third straight weekly decline.

Volkswagen fell 5.6% after it lowered its operating profit margin outlook following a sharp contraction in its market. Nestle dropped 2.6% after Russia took over local assets of Nestle and French supermarket chain Auchan. Airtel Africa Plc's London-listed shares tumbled 11% as the company considers reducing the size of the fundraising for an Airtel Money initial public offering below the amount it had previously sought.

data.title: Bakkt Shares Rise 8.45% as Crypto-Linked Equities Rally
data.description: Bakkt shares rose 8.45% to $8.09 on Friday as crypto-linked equities moved higher. According to NS3.AI, Bitcoin's surge reflected renewed optimism about U.S. digital asset regulation after the Clarity Act recently failed in the Senate.

data.description: Fire crews responded Friday to a blaze at Vistra Corp.’s damaged battery storage facility in California, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: XRP Rises 6.93% as Bitcoin Reclaims $80,000 and Dominance Falls
data.description:
XRP rose 6.93% on the daily candle as Bitcoin recovered above $80,000. According to NS3.AI, the move narrowed the gap between XRP's 50-day and 200-day exponential moving averages, although a daily golden cross has not been confirmed.

Bitcoin's dominance also fell from 64% to 59% as traders rotated into smaller tokens.

data.title: STOCKS | Robinhood Shares Rise 8.58% as CFTC and SEC Ease Market Access Rules
data.description:
Robinhood shares rose 8.58% to $119.23 on Friday alongside Bitcoin. According to NS3.AI, the CFTC cleared a path for passive software providers to connect users with regulated derivatives products without registering as brokers, provided they avoid handling customer funds and trade execution.

The SEC also opened a temporary five-year window for approved venues to offer tokenized U.S. stocks. Separately, the CLARITY Act fell 11 votes short of the 60 needed to advance in the Senate.

data.title: Saudi Security Delegation Reportedly Met Mossad and Israeli Military Intelligence Chiefs
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Palestinian sources disclosed via the Iranian Students' News Agency (ISNA) that a Saudi senior security and military delegation met with the heads of Mossad and Israeli military intelligence under the supervision of U.S. Central Command, seeking support for operations against the Houthis.

data.title: STOCKS | MARA Holdings Rises 8.93% as Bitcoin Climbs and Crypto-Linked Shares Advance
data.description: MARA Holdings shares rose 8.93% to $12.68 at publication on Friday, while Bitcoin traded at $80,997.20 after gaining 6.09% over 24 hours. According to NS3.AI, Morgan Stanley maintained an Underweight rating on MARA and lifted its price forecast to $11. Shares of other crypto-linked companies also moved higher after a CFTC proposal on crypto market regulation.

data.title: Empower's Marta Norton Says Retirement Investors Are on Autopilot
data.description: Marta Norton, chief investment strategist at Empower, said retirement investors are "on autopilot" while discussing the outlook for equities and retirement investing amid a bond selloff and rate-hiking cycle, according to Bloomberg.
